source_text: [1] Ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν τὸ ἴδιον ἐποίουν ὡς ἄνθρωπος εἰς ἕνωσιν κατηρτισμένος. οὗ δὲ μερισμός ἐστιν καὶ ὀργή. θεὸς οὐ κατοικεῖ. πᾶσιν οὖν μετανοοῦσιν ἀφίει ὁ κύριος, ἐὰν μετανοήσωσιν εἰς ἑνότητα θεοῦ καὶ συνέδριον τοῦ ἐπισκόπου. πιστεύω τῇ χάριτι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὃς λύσει ἀφ̓ ὑμῶν πάντα δεσμόν. [2] παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς μηδὲν κατ’ ἐριθείαν πράσσειν, ἀλλὰ κατὰ χριστομαθίαν. ἐπεὶ ἤκουσά τινων λεγόντων, ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ ἐν τοῖς ἀρχείοις εὕρω ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ οὐ πιστεύω: καὶ λέγοντός μου αὐτοῖς ὅτι γέγραπται, ἀπεκρίθησάν μοι ὅτι πρόκειται. ἐμοὶ δὲ ἀρχεῖά ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, τὰ ἄθικτα ἀρχεῖα ὁ σταυρὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ ὁ θάνατος καὶ ἡ ἀνάστασις αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ πίστις ἡ δἰ αὐτοῦ, ἐν οἶς θέλω ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ ὑμῶν δικαιωθῆναι.
pass_a_gloss: So I was doing my own part, as a man fitted for unity. Where there is division and anger, God does not dwell. So the Lord forgives all who repent, if they repent and turn to the unity of God and the council of the bishop. I trust in the grace of Jesus Christ, who will loose every bond from you. And I urge you to do nothing out of rivalry, but according to what you have learned of Christ. For I heard some saying, If I do not find it in the archives, I do not believe it in the gospel. And when I said to them, It is written, they answered me, That is the question. But for me the archives are Jesus Christ; the untouchable archives are his cross and death and his resurrection and the faith that comes through him; in these I want to be justified, by your prayer.

lemmas.gloss: learning of Christ, discipleship in Christ
lie before; be the question at issue

pass_b_english: My part, then, I did, as a man made for unity. Where division and anger are, God does not dwell. To all who repent the Lord grants forgiveness, if in repenting they turn to the unity of God and to the bishop's council. I trust the grace of Jesus Christ to loose you from every chain.

Here is my plea: act from no spirit of rivalry (Philippians 2:3), but as those taught by Christ. I heard some people saying, "Unless I find it in the archives, I don't believe it in the gospel." I told them, "It is written." Their reply: "That is exactly what is in dispute." But my archives are Jesus Christ. His cross, his death, his resurrection, and the faith that comes through him: these are the archives no one can tamper with. By these, through your prayer, I long to be justified.

choices.why: Public records or charters; the opponents mean the Old Testament as the authority on file.

anf_compare.notes: ANF construes the opponents' words as 'If I do not find it in the ancient Scriptures, I will not believe the Gospel'; the supplied Greek (no comma) reads more naturally 'I do not believe it in the gospel', and ἀρχεῖα are archives, not 'ancient Scriptures' in so many words. ANF 'communion with the bishop' for συνέδριον (council). Overall argument the same.

notes: The punctuation of the opponents' sentence is disputed among editors; this follows the supplied Lake text, which has no comma before ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ.
Source shows 'ἀφ̓', 'δἰ', and 'οἶς' (for οἷς); reproduced as supplied.

review.notes: Source identity confirmed: Ignatius Philadelphians 8 from Lake 1912 Loeb edition. Completeness: all clauses from the single Greek paragraph are rendered in both Pass A and B, including the archival dispute, divine unity, forgiveness conditional on repentance and turn to God's unity and bishop's council, trust in Christ's grace to loose bonds, avoidance of rivalry, appeal to Christ's teaching, opponents' argument about archives vs gospel, response 'it is written', their rebuttal 'that is the question', and Ignatius' affirmation that Christ is the true archives (cross, death, resurrection, faith) in which he seeks justification through their prayer. Negation: 'God does not dwell' (θεὸς οὐ κατοικεῖ) correctly negated in both Pass A and B. Agency: Lord forgives (ἀφίει ὁ κύριος), Christ loosens (λύσει), opponents speak/answer, Ignatius urges/trusts/wants justified — all properly attributed. Modality: conditional 'if they repent' (ἐὰν μετανοήσωσιν) preserved; imperative 'I urge' (παρακαλῶ) rendered; declarative/assertive statements maintained. Doctrine: Ignatius' Christological archives (cross, death, resurrection, faith) and their role in justification before God via prayer is accurately conveyed. Scripture: inline citation (Philippians 2:3) correctly attached to 'μηδὲν κατ’ ἐριθείαν πράσσειν' in both Pass A and B per bible_refs and notes; matches supplied wording. Title 'My Archives Are Jesus Christ' names the thought (Ignatius' redefinition of divine authority), not just locus. Pass A fidelity: every clause's sense preserved (e.g., 'turn to the unity of God and the council of the bishop' matches συνέδριον τοῦ ἐπισκόπου; 'loose every bond from you' matches λύσει ἀφ̓ ὑμῶν πάντα δεσμόν). Pass B adds no contradictions: 'turn to the unity of God and to the bishop's council' equivalent; 'loose you from every chain' equivalent to 'loose every bond from you'; Phil 2:3 gloss added as permissible elucidation; 'archives no one can tamper with' reflects ἄθικτα; 'I long to be justified' conveys future-oriented δικαιωθῆναι with Ignatius' desire. No uncertainties; all supplied Greek accounted for. Covered source paragraphs: [1].
